context:
Goal: each session starts on current main, so it never reads stale rules or code.
Problem (rule): the start hook cannot tell whether another live session shares a clean main checkout, so it can move files under that session, and your Q6 answer left this nuance for you to decide.
Based on (ruling): your 21:59 CST Nov 12 answer, "Q6 B — but theres probs some nuance here ponder it!" (ruling fast-forward-clean-start); the never-shared clause is the retrospective's proposal, not your words.
Based on (read): hooks/session_start.sh in PR #3141 refuses only agent worktrees, so a second session's start in a shared clean main checkout moves files under the first session.
Departs from: main, which never fast-forwards at start — adds a fast-forward of a clean checkout, in every clean checkout (a) or only in a session's own linked worktree (b).

options.gain: No liveness tracking to build; a plain main clone stays current too.
options.how: PR #3141 stays as it is: any clean checkout on the default branch fast-forwards at start, except agent worktrees.
options.label: Keep as built (recommended)
options.lose: A second session's start can change files under a first session in the same clean main checkout. Nothing is lost, since the tree was clean, but the first session reads newer files mid-task.

options.gain: A shared checkout never moves under a running session.
options.how: Fast-forward only in a linked worktree under .claude/worktrees/ that is not an agent worktree; a plain main clone never moves.
options.label: Only a session's own linked worktree
options.lose: A plain main clone, such as the pointer checkout, never fast-forwards, so a session started there can read stale main.

shown.label: Only a session's own linked worktree

title: May a session's start fast-forward a clean main checkout that another live session may share?
why: Your 21:59 CST Nov 12 answer (Q6 B) asked for the nuance to be pondered; this is that nuance, and no ruling of yours settles it.
